body_markdown:
Softgen reports more than 186,000 builders using its AI-powered web app platform. However, teams looking for different pricing structures, mobile publishing options, and familiar AI development workflows may want to consider alternatives.[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants.


This guide compares seven Softgen alternatives for non-technical founders, small business owners, and teams seeking to[build full-stack apps](https://floot.com/blog/how-to-build-full-stack-app-with-ai) with AI. It examines development workflows, backend infrastructure, mobile capabilities, pricing, and code ownership to help you choose a platform that fits your project.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Build inside familiar AI tools:** Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) works with Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, allowing users to develop apps through supported AI assistants.
- **Get managed full-stack infrastructure:** Floot includes[built-in services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) such as Postgres, authentication, storage, email, hosting, and payment integrations.
- **Create web and mobile apps:** Floot supports[mobile app builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) for iOS and Android, with cloud-based builds and supported app-store testing uploads.
- **Understand the complete pricing model:** Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , with build-action limits, hosting allowances, separate AI credits, and paid plans for higher usage.
- **Maintain ownership of your work:** Floot users[own their code](https://floot.com/blog/do-you-own-your-code-on-floot) and app data on every plan, with database export available on Free and full project ZIP downloads on paid plans.


## **Understanding AI App Builders and Their Cost Structures**


AI app builders allow users to describe software requirements in natural language instead of manually writing every component. However, subscription prices do not always reflect the full cost of developing, launching, and operating an application. The main differences involve how AI development is billed, which backend services are included, and whether additional tools are required to publish and maintain the finished app.


When comparing platforms, consider these factors:


- **AI development costs:** Some platforms charge per credit, message, or token, while others provide monthly allowances. Floot's[connector-based development](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) uses the connected AI assistant's existing model access rather than a separate Floot AI build-credit charge.
- **Hosting and backend infrastructure:** Apps may require databases, authentication, file storage, and deployment services. Platforms offering[managed infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) reduce the amount of manual configuration.
- **Mobile publishing:** Some builders focus on web applications, while others offer native mobile projects or app-store packaging. Floot's[mobile publishing workflow](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) includes cloud builds and testing-track uploads.
- **Code ownership and portability:** GitHub synchronization, project downloads, and database exports differ between platforms. Floot's[code export options](https://floot.com/blog/do-you-own-your-code-on-floot) distinguish ownership from the paid ability to download a complete project.
- **Ongoing usage expenses:** Hosting traffic, database activity, AI features inside published apps, payment processing, and external services may create additional charges beyond a subscription.


Softgen offers a free trial followed by credit-based subscriptions. Its Starter plan costs $25/month with 500 credits, while Pro costs $49/month with 1,500 credits. Additional credits can be purchased when necessary. Repeated prompts and complex changes may increase credit consumption, making development usage an important consideration alongside the monthly plan fee.


## **1. Floot**


Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) that lets users create, edit, test, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations.


The connected AI assistant handles development within its available connector permissions, while Floot provides managed infrastructure, including databases, authentication, storage, and hosting. This allows builders to work through familiar AI conversations rather than managing separate infrastructure services.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **AI assistant integration:** Build and edit applications through Claude, Codex, Cursor, compatible ChatGPT configurations, and other supported AI clients using Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) .
- **Connector-based development:** Connected AI assistants handle application development, with available capabilities depending on each client's connector permissions.
- **Managed backend infrastructure:** Create full-stack applications with persistent databases, authentication, file storage, and hosting using Floot's[built-in services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) .
- **Web-to-mobile conversion:** Turn hosted web applications into installable iOS and Android apps using[mobile app builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) .
- **Cloud-based mobile builds:** Generate mobile builds without requiring a local Mac, Xcode, or Android Studio installation.
- **App-store testing uploads:** Upload builds to[TestFlight and Google Play](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) internal testing using connected developer accounts, subject to Floot plan requirements.


### **Built-In Services**


Floot provides[managed application infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) that reduces the need for extensive external service configuration:


- **Database:** Managed Postgres with SQL access, a browser-based table view, and database export on all plans.
- **Authentication:** Email/password login and supported OAuth sign-in options, including Google and Microsoft.
- **File storage:** Public and private file handling with CDN-backed asset delivery.
- **Email and notifications:** Transactional email services and support for push notifications.
- **Payments:**[Built-in Stripe payments](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/payments) for one-time purchases and subscriptions. Testing is available on Free, while real payments require Pro or Power. Stripe processing fees apply, alongside a 1% Floot fee on Pro and no additional Floot percentage fee on Power.
- **Hosting:** Managed hosting with SSL, live application URLs, and usage-based infrastructure allowances.
- **SEO:**[Server-side pre-rendering](https://floot.com/en/seo) , sitemap support, robots.txt controls, and page metadata management.


Some services, including live payments and app-store publishing, require users to connect their own external accounts.


### **Pricing**


Floot is free to start, with three main plans listed on its[pricing page](https://floot.com/en/pricing) :


- **Free ($0/month):** 100 build actions per day, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, a one-time $3 hosting credit valid for one year, and 2 mobile builds per month. The Free plan has no recurring monthly hosting allowance.
- **Pro ($25/month):** 1,000 build actions per day, 5,000 monthly AI credits, $10/month hosting allowance, 12 mobile builds per month, custom domains, and priority support.
- **Power ($100/month):** 5,000 build actions per day, 15,000 monthly AI credits, $25/month hosting allowance, unlimited mobile builds, and all Pro features.


Annual billing offers two months free.


Connector-based development uses the connected AI assistant's model access and does not consume Floot AI build credits. Floot separately meters build actions. Optional Floot AI agent usage, image generation, and AI features within published applications can consume Floot AI credits.


Hosting is usage-based. Beyond the included allowances, costs draw from prepaid hosting credit, with optional auto-reload on eligible paid plans.


### **Why Floot Stands Out for Full-Stack App Development**


Floot is designed for non-technical founders, operators, and business owners who need working applications with user accounts and saved data.


Users retain ownership of their code and data on every plan. Database export is available on Free plan, while full project ZIP downloads require a paid plan.


Floot has a[4.8/5 G2 rating](https://www.g2.com/products/floot/reviews) , based on eight reviews as of November 16, 2026. Its Y Combinator profile reports growth from 5 to[600+ paying customers](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/floot/jobs) during the Summer 2025 batch. This is a historical early-growth figure, not Floot's current customer count.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable is a conversational AI app builder focused on creating and refining web applications. It combines AI-assisted development with visual editing, cloud services, and a credit-based subscription model.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Visual application editing:** AI-assisted creation and refinement of application interfaces.
- **Credit-based development:** Monthly build credits, daily grants, and additional credit top-ups.
- **GitHub synchronization:** Two-way synchronization for version control and code portability.
- **Backend services:** Lovable Cloud provides database, authentication, and hosting functionality, with Supabase integration also available.


### **Platform Considerations**


Lovable primarily builds responsive web applications rather than native iOS or Android projects. Teams requiring app-store distribution need an additional mobile development or packaging workflow.


Its GitHub integration supports users who want to manage code through external development tools.


Builders considering both platforms can also review Floot's[Lovable comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-lovable-compare-ai-no-code-platforms-2025) for additional context, while checking current features and pricing.


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new, developed by StackBlitz, is a browser-based AI application builder using WebContainers technology. It supports multiple JavaScript frameworks and provides an interactive development environment.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Multiple framework support:** React, Vue, Svelte, Astro, and other supported web frameworks.
- **Token-based development:** AI interactions consume tokens according to usage and project complexity.
- **Browser-based environment:** Application development and testing occur in the browser.
- **GitHub integration:** Code export and synchronization capabilities.
- **Backend services:** Built-in cloud database and hosting functionality.


### **Platform Considerations**


Bolt.new can generate Expo-based React Native projects for mobile development. Mobile app-store publishing uses the associated Expo and EAS build and submission workflow.


Token consumption varies with the size and complexity of a project, so extensive code generation and repeated modifications can affect available usage.


For more context on the two approaches, see Floot's[Bolt comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-bolt-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) .


## **4. Replit**


Replit combines a cloud-based development environment with AI assistance through Replit Agent. It supports application creation, code editing, testing, and deployment within one workspace.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Complete development environment:** IDE functionality with terminal access and development tools.
- **Multiple programming languages:** Support for more than 50 languages.
- **AI development assistance:** Replit Agent supports conversational development and automated coding tasks.
- **Usage-based credits:** Included AI usage allowances with additional usage-based charges.
- **Integrated deployment:** Applications can be hosted through Replit's deployment services.


### **Platform Considerations**


Replit provides direct access to development tools, which can benefit users who want to inspect and modify application code. Its IDE-based workflow may require more familiarity with software development concepts than a purely conversational interface.


Replit Agent also supports Expo-based mobile development, with app-store deployment requiring the appropriate build and publishing process.


Floot's[Replit comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-replit-compare-ai-vibecoding-platforms-in-2026) provides additional context for evaluating different development workflows.


## **5. Base44**


Base44, acquired by Wix in 2025, offers AI-powered application building with integrated backend services and a credit-based subscription structure.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Backend infrastructure:** Built-in authentication, database functionality, storage, and hosting.
- **Message credits:** Monthly allowances for AI-assisted development.
- **Custom domains:** Available on eligible paid plans.
- **GitHub integration:** Code export and synchronization on Builder and higher plans.
- **Mobile packaging:** Tools for preparing iOS and Android app-store files.


### **Platform Considerations**


Base44 supports packaging published web applications into iOS and Android app-store files using a native WebView shell. Downloading app-store submission files requires an eligible paid plan, and developers remain responsible for their store accounts and final submissions.


Its integrated backend services can reduce initial setup work for web applications, while message credits and integration allowances remain important when estimating costs.


For a related comparison, see Floot's[Base44 comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-base44-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) .


## **6. Bubble**


Bubble is an established visual application development platform that combines no-code workflows with AI-assisted creation and editing.


The platform supports web applications and native mobile app development, with its native mobile builder becoming generally available in November 2026.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Visual workflow editor:** Drag-and-drop tools for building application logic and interfaces.
- **Plugin marketplace:** Third-party integrations and additional functionality.
- **Backend infrastructure:** Integrated databases, hosting, and application workflows.
- **AI development tools:** AI-assisted application creation and editing.
- **Native mobile support:** iOS and Android application development alongside web apps.
- **Workload-based pricing:** Resource usage measured through workload units.


### **Platform Considerations**


Bubble combines visual programming with AI assistance. Builders can generate applications with AI tools and refine their interfaces and logic using the visual editor. Its workflow model provides detailed control over application behavior, but users need to learn Bubble's development environment.


The platform suits teams comfortable with visual development tools who require database-backed applications, custom workflows, and integrations.


## **7. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets eligible ChatGPT users build, publish, and share interactive websites and lightweight web applications.


It combines conversational development with hosted web experiences, data storage, and configurable sharing controls.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Conversational development:** Create and refine websites and lightweight applications using ChatGPT and Codex.
- **Built-in hosting:** Publish applications without separately configuring a hosting provider.
- **Persistent storage:** Store application data and uploaded files.
- **Visitor access controls:** Configure private, workspace, or public access where supported.
- **Custom domains:** Connect an existing domain where the feature is available.
- **Connected applications:** Supported workspace configurations can use visitors' authorized app connections.


### **Platform Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites is designed for interactive websites, dashboards, resource hubs, internal tools, and lightweight applications. It supports persistent data and visitor-access controls, but the supported runtime and available features depend on the user's plan and workspace configuration.


Its publishing workflow focuses on hosted web applications rather than providing a native iOS and Android app-store distribution workflow. Floot provides a complementary option for users who want managed Postgres infrastructure, authentication, payments, email services, and mobile publishing while continuing to develop through compatible AI assistants.


## **When Is Floot the Right Softgen Alternative?**


Floot is a suitable option for non-technical founders, business owners, and operators who already use supported AI assistants and want to publish working applications without manually managing infrastructure. Its MCP connector lets the connected assistant handle development, while Floot provides hosting and backend services.


The platform is particularly relevant when you need:


- **An existing AI workflow:** Build through Claude, Codex, Cursor, or a compatible ChatGPT configuration using[Floot's connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) .
- **Persistent application data:** Use a[managed Postgres database](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) with authentication and storage.
- **Web and mobile publishing:** Create hosted web apps and[mobile builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) for supported app-store testing.
- **Code and data ownership:** Retain ownership with[export options](https://floot.com/blog/do-you-own-your-code-on-floot) suited to different plans.


Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , but building limits, hosting usage, optional AI features, and developer-account fees should be considered when planning a project. The[community showcase](https://floot.com/en/showcase) provides examples of applications built using the platform.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the main difference between Floot and Softgen for AI app building?**


Floot is a[full-stack app platform](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/how-floot-works) with an MCP connector that works through supported AI assistants. The connected assistant handles application development within its connector permissions, while Floot manages infrastructure. Softgen provides its own AI-building environment with monthly development credits and optional top-ups. Floot connector-based development does not create a separate Floot AI build-credit charge, although AI subscription costs, build-action limits, hosting usage, and optional AI features remain separate considerations.


### **Can Floot build mobile apps for iOS and Android?**


Yes. Floot can convert web applications into installable iOS and Android apps using native shells and cloud builds. Its[app-store workflow](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) supports uploading builds to TestFlight and Google Play internal testing. Apple account connection is supported on every Floot plan, while Google Play connection requires a paid plan. Publishing requires an Apple Developer Program membership costing $99 per year for iOS or a Google Play developer account costing $25 as a one-time fee for Android. Users must complete final app-store submissions themselves. Apple and Google independently review applications, so approval is not guaranteed.


### **What backend infrastructure does Floot provide?**


Floot provides[managed infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) including Postgres databases, user authentication, file storage, transactional email, hosting, and support for payments and scheduled jobs. Users can build applications with logins, saved records, backend workflows, and integrations without manually configuring every underlying service. The platform also offers[SEO tools](https://floot.com/en/seo) , including pre-rendering, sitemap and robots.txt controls, and page metadata. These can improve crawlability but do not guarantee indexing or rankings.


### **Do users own the applications they build with Floot?**


Yes. Floot states that users own their application code, data, and intellectual property on every plan. Its[code ownership guide](https://floot.com/blog/do-you-own-your-code-on-floot) explains the available export options. Database export is available on Free, while complete project ZIP downloads require a paid plan. Exporting application code does not automatically recreate Floot's managed services on another hosting provider. Users moving elsewhere may need to replace platform-specific integrations and configure their own infrastructure.


### **How much does it cost to start building apps with Floot?**


Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , with 100 daily build actions, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, a one-time $3 hosting credit valid for one year, and 2 mobile builds per month. Pro costs $25/month with 1,000 daily build actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, a $10 monthly hosting allowance, and 12 mobile builds. Power costs $100/month with 5,000 daily actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, a $25 hosting allowance, and unlimited mobile builds. Building through a connected AI assistant uses that assistant's model access rather than separate Floot AI build credits. Hosting overages, optional AI features, external AI subscriptions, and applicable developer-account fees should be budgeted separately.
